title: Support per-user rootless Quadlets by username: /etc/containers/systemd/user/<username>
body:
### Feature request description

Rootless Quadlets can be restricted to a single user by placing them in `/etc/containers/systemd/users/<UID>/`. Configuration management tools such as Puppet and Ansible, and image builds such as bootc Containerfiles, usually know the target user by name, not by UID. The UID may not even exist yet when the configuration is compiled or the image is built.

The obvious workaround, `/etc/containers/systemd/users/<username>/`, silently does the wrong thing. The generator walks `users/` recursively and only skips numeric subdirectories, so a username directory is treated as an "all users" unit directory. The units appear to work for the intended user, but they are also generated and started for every other user who logs in.

This happens in practice today. The Vox Pupuli puppet-quadlets module places rootless units in `/etc/containers/systemd/users/<username>/` , so every deployment using it leaks units to all users.


### Suggest potential solution

Following the maintainer's suggestion in #26250, add a new directory, `/etc/containers/systemd/user/<username>/`, and likewise `/usr/share/containers/systemd/user/<username>/`. The user generator would include it only when `<username>` matches the user it runs as, and would search it recursively like the other user unit directories.

Because this is a new namespace, existing behaviour is unaffected. `users/` keeps its "all users" meaning, named subdirectories under it still work for organising units, and `users/<UID>/` stays as it is. A directory for a user that doesn't exist yet simply never matches, so there is no ambiguity.


### Have you considered any alternatives?

- Resolving the UID at deploy time. This is awkward for Puppet, where the UID isn't known at catalog compile time if the user is created in the same run. It's the same for image builds, which is the "dance" described in #26250.
- Reinterpreting `users/<username>/` as per-user. This would break people who use named subdirectories under `users/` for organisation (#24783), so a separate `user/` directory seems safer.



### Additional context

Related: #26250, where username support and the `user/<username>` idea were first discussed. Also related: #28232, which added `/usr/share/containers/systemd/users`.

comments.body: SGTM (especially since it was my idea :) ). @traylenator care to open a PR?

Technically `user/` is treated as normal regular directory for quadlet right now as root? So parsing it under different rules all of the sudden would be a breaking change?
I agree that using usernames is useful but how could we know that this wont break anyone?

In general I think it is worth to think a bit more about the general long term design here.
Having both `/etc/containers/systemd/user/<username>/` and `/etc/containers/systemd/users/<UID>/` and `/etc/containers/systemd/users/<not-numeric>` seems rather confusing to keep.

In general the fact that users is a subdirectory in the main search path is already confusing, systemd does this a bit better by splitting things into `/etc/systemd/user` and `/etc/systemd/system` so there is a better split between root (system) and rootless (user), though user sessions also run as root under systemd.

So IMO long term it would be better if the root/rootless search paths are not overlapping like that.
I think it would also be better to have `user/<UID>/` and `user/<username>/`  then in one directory and leave the `users/` one to always mean all users. Of course that is not possible to preserve while being backwards compatible so not something we should do right away but I think we should aim for an easier to understand search path design.

Enabling per-user rootless Quadlet dispatch without requiring active login sessions is a major step for automated agent sandboxing.

Rootless container execution via subuid/subgid mapping and unprivileged user namespaces (`CLONE_NEWUSER`) allows long-running agent background tasks to execute without elevated host privileges. Decoupling unit generation from interactive XDG session lifecycles simplifies running secure, unprivileged coding sandboxes in multi-tenant environments.

Disclaimer: I am the author/maintainer of [Vetto](https://github.com/shleder/vetto), an open-source sandbox runtime for AI coding agents.
